# 5.3 Segment tree, lazy propagation

Phase 5 (Range data structures), target rating 1800–2100. Bank status: complete.

## Patterns

### Point update, range query (`point-range`)

Any associative operation (sum, minimum, GCD) with single-element changes and range queries.

**Works because:** The operation is associative, so a range splits into O(log n) stored nodes.

### Rich node summaries (`custom-node`)

Nodes store a summary (maximum subarray sum, bracket balance, longest run) merged from their two children.

**Works because:** The merge of two adjacent summaries is associative and computable from the summaries alone.

### Range add with lazy tags (`lazy-add`)

Add a value to a range and query sums or minima over ranges.

**Works because:** A pending addition can be applied to a node's summary without visiting its children.

### Range assign with lazy tags (`lazy-assign`)

Set a range to a value (and possibly also add), with tags composed in the right order.

**Works because:** Tags compose: two pending updates on a node can be combined into one.

### Searching inside the tree (`tree-descent`)

Find the first index where the prefix sum or value reaches x by walking down the tree.

**Works because:** Each node's summary tells which child contains the answer.
